method: offline Unicorn run over the memory image; nothing hooked out; a code hook asserts execution stays inside the query, the support routine, the vector leaves and __chkstk (the static-initialiser cold paths are excluded and never reached)
fixtures: XYZ mask {-1,-1,-1,0} at 0x3336890; 1 query case in 16 uses a random mask
TEB+0x10 StackLimit for __chkstk 0x1c45120; TEB+0x58 TLS array, epoch 1 at block+0x4eec
statics 0x3336a30/0x3336a50/0x3336a70 = 1e-7 x4 (initializer values), guards 0x3336a40/60/80 = 1; about 8% of query cases use other static values (zero, random) against the model parameter

hulls: random clouds, boxes, flat, collinear, duplicate-vertex, single-vertex, tetrahedra, sphere samples, 1..48 vertices; +0x48 = n+1 (constructor convention) in ~85%, else n; the padding slot holds random bytes; ~20% use a synthetic cube-map support table (+0xc0/+0xd0/+0xe0..e8)
frames: random rotations (15% non-orthonormal scaled), random translation, lane 3 random in 30%; iterations 16 in ~85%, else one of 0, -1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 100
comparisons: all 0x60 bytes at out (0x30 written: distance, hull point, point-side point; the rest unchanged)
block, point, shape, vertex, table and list bytes unchanged
support routine return index (32-bit) for random directions
composed: sphere entry return value and every region (record bytes, inputs) bit-exact
bit-exact float32 lanes under the emulator two-NaN rule (x87)
limits: Two-NaN lanes compared under nan_rule x87 (QEMU softfloat); the manual SSE rule differs in the counted cases.
MXCSR is the Unicorn default 0x1f80 (round to nearest, no FTZ/DAZ); the live MXCSR is not established.

Synthetic hulls and support tables; no live shapes. The deserialisation path that fills hull arrays (default constructor 0x18af470) was not traced; the count-1 verdict rests on the constructor 0x1948780 and the clone path 0x1948e20.
The CRT static-initialiser paths (0x1c44fb0/0x1c44f50) are supplied, not run: statics are fixtures.
No rsqrtps/rcpps are executed by this routine; nothing here depends on hardware approximations.
